body.en: The EST I tests right-triangle trigonometry, radian measure, and basic complex numbers. These appear mostly in Section II.

In a right triangle, the hypotenuse is 13 and one leg is 5. Find \( \sin\theta \) for the angle opposite the leg of length 12. \[ \text{other leg}=\sqrt{13^2-5^2}=12,\quad \sin\theta=\frac{12}{13}. \]

body.en:
Complex numbers

A complex number has the form \( a+bi \) where \( i=\sqrt{-1} \). Add by combining real and imaginary parts separately: \( (3+2i)+(1-5i)=4-3i \). Multiply using FOIL and replace \( i^2 \) with \( -1 \).

SOH-CAH-TOA: \(\sin\theta = \text{opp}/\text{hyp}\), \(\cos\theta = \text{adj}/\text{hyp}\), \(\tan\theta = \text{opp}/\text{adj}\). Pythagorean identity: \(\sin^2\theta + \cos^2\theta = 1\). Exact values: \(\sin 30° = \tfrac{1}{2}\), \(\cos 30° = \tfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\), \(\sin 45° = \tfrac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\). Complex: \(i^2 = -1\); \(|a+bi| = \sqrt{a^2+b^2}\).

label.en: Worked example — Finding all sides of a right triangle

body.en:
In right triangle, the hypotenuse is 13 and one angle is \(22.6°\). Find the other two sides.

Opposite \(= 13\sin 22.6° \approx 13 \times 0.3843 \approx 5\). Adjacent \(= 13\cos 22.6° \approx 12\).

label.en: ▲ EST I Math Traps & Pitfalls — Trigonometry & Additional Topics

body.en:
• Radian vs. Degree Mode: If evaluating trigonometric ratios on a calculator, always verify your active mode! Evaluating \(\sin(30)\) in radian mode yields \(-0.988\) instead of \(0.5\).
  • Complementary Angle Theorem: In any right triangle, the acute angles sum to \(90^\circ\), which implies \(\sin(x) = \cos(90^\circ - x)\) and \(\cos(x) = \sin(90^\circ - x)\). If \(\sin(A) = \cos(B)\), then \(A + B = 90^\circ\).
  • Pythagorean Identity Variations: \(\sin^2\theta + \cos^2\theta = 1\) rearranges to \(\sin^2\theta = 1 - \cos^2\theta = (1 - \cos\theta)(1 + \cos\theta)\). Recognizing this difference of squares simplifies many algebraic trig questions instantly.
  • Powers of \(i\) Cyclicity: Powers of the imaginary unit cycle every 4 powers: \(i^1 = i\), \(i^2 = -1\), \(i^3 = -i\), \(i^4 = 1\). To evaluate \(i^n\), divide \(n\) by 4 and use the remainder.

question.en: In a right triangle with acute angles \(A\) and \(B\), it is given that \(\sin(3x + 10^\circ) = \cos(2x + 15^\circ)\). (a) Find the value of \(x\). (b) Determine the value of \(\tan(x + 5^\circ)\).

solution.en:
(a) Use complementary angle identity: Since \(\sin A = \cos B\) for acute angles in a right triangle, \(A + B = 90^\circ\): \[ (3x + 10^\circ) + (2x + 15^\circ) = 90^\circ \implies 5x + 25^\circ = 90^\circ \implies 5x = 65^\circ \implies x = 13^\circ. \]

(b) Evaluate tangent: Substitute \(x = 13^\circ\): \[ \tan(13^\circ + 5^\circ) = \tan(18^\circ) \approx 0.3249. \]
